title: The fedora's name
hook: The fedora is named after a stage heroine, and it started out as a women's hat.
peek: In 1882 a French play called Fédora opened in Paris, with Sarah Bernhardt in the title role. The soft, creased hat she wore took the play's name, long before it became a classic men's hat.
lede: The fedora takes its name from Fédora, an 1882 play by the French writer Victorien Sardou. The star was Sarah Bernhardt, the most famous actress of her day, playing a Russian princess called Fédora. In the usual account, her soft felt hat with a creased crown caught on, and fedora became the name for the style, first taken up by women.

bullets.text: Sardou wrote the play for Bernhardt, and it was a big success. It is a high-drama tale of a princess and a lost love, and it later inspired an opera, Fedora, by Umberto Giordano in 1898.
Bernhardt was a fashion leader as well as a star, and audiences copied what she wore. The soft hat named after her role became a women's fashion in the 1880s and 1890s.
A fedora has a soft brim and a crown with a lengthwise crease and two pinches at the front. Its soft felt was a change from stiff men's hats like the top hat and the bowler.
By the early 1900s men had adopted the fedora. Prince Edward, later Edward VIII, is often credited with making it fashionable in the 1920s, and it became a standard men's hat for decades.
